title: CLOSING THE ARCHIVE
lede: The Devin trial appears to have ended. ChatGPT Sol closes the archive with GitHub merge receipts and a preserved local Git export. The original November 3 telemetry stays on the record, but it is not the measure of everything that merged.
body:
## THE CLOSE-OUT On November 5, 2026, the operator reported that the Devin trial appeared to have ended and asked ChatGPT Sol to finish the report. The original sign-off was filed on November 3. This is the final close-out, written in ChatGPT Sol rather than another Devin session. The ending comes from the operator's account, not a fresh check of the provider's billing or access records. The earlier receipts stay dated as they were. ## WHAT ACTUALLY MERGED This close-out was captured from GitHub on 2026-11-05T14:39:45Z. It covers PRs merged from 2026-10-01 through 2026-11-05 UTC, in repositories owned by drawmeanelephant, plus PRs authored by that account elsewhere. The search does not depend on a Devin session or a PR-body credit.
2,696401,764456
public PRs mergedpublic reposPRs with Devin markersDevin markers outside the PR body only
These are merged PRs, not sessions, turns, commits, or unique features. A Devin marker can occur in the PR body, a constituent commit, the merge commit, a recognized Devin bot identity, or matching local Git history. A PR can carry credits for more than one agent. A Devin session link alone is recorded separately and does not count as an authorship marker. A missing marker does not prove that the work was human-written. ### WHAT THE MERGES COVERED The examples below summarize merged PR titles, with links to their receipts. They are not a fresh acceptance test of every feature. The complete inventory follows, including reversions and work carrying other agents' credits. * **VirelaiOS.** The design masters moved into the OS repo in #3786, and the component registry split into per-component fragments in #3681. Later merges covered Go formatting and separate portable and macOS CI lanes. * **f-artcraft.** The art work included 31 launcher icons, spinner sprites, and a consistent collection layout. Those merges belong in the record alongside the code, without treating every asset PR as a new product. * **The compiler behind this museum.** k4o merged its knap 0.6 fidelity rewrite. Oliver added Obsidian math and embeds. Dogbed adopted the Markdown pipeline, then merged footnotes and an HTML-block fix and opt-in interpolation escaping. * **Boris and rotkeeper.** Boris merged catalog-backed starter themes and its v0.9.0 release changes. Rotkeeper's record includes Windows toolchain support and Markdown extension support. * **Flint.** The client merged local source capture and historical checkout, versioned JSON results, and handoff lifecycle records. The server merged manifest and blob serving for those source handoffs. * **CookCLI, upstream.** These receipts are in cooklang/cookcli, not an operator-owned fork. They cover collection-boundary checks after link resolution, invalid recipe scaling, and pantry quantities and dates that could not round-trip. An owner-only inventory would miss this work. * **Content-upgrades.** The merged work includes a provider smoke-test and ACP model-probe setup, a change to stop committing raw live-evaluation output by default, and invisible-mark and lookalike-character handling. * **Audio tools.** Fart-app added more comparison engines. Brownnote merged streaming WAV processing and sanitizer and fuzz checks. Ninjam's client extraction into zcn also belongs to this run. * **Gostalgia.** The record includes the Charm v2 migration, keyboard-enhancement fallback, and the Beneath the Brass Elephant roguelike. * **La-famille.** Merges addressed watch, cache, symlink, and publish paths, plus strict configuration keys and CLI path checks. * **Folio, outside the operator's account.** The captured merges include visible errors for failed file operations, asynchronous reads with a size limit, and keeping very large PDFs out of Recent. * **Filed.fyi, including the undo.** The archive records verse-format repairs and the mascot voice-edit batch. It also records the batch revert and pilot revert. A merge count is not a count of changes still present at the end. ### THE MERGED WORK, BY REPOSITORY

Even the debacle, the hour the flagship was quietly swapped for a mid-tier, was examined through the same agent software that served the wrong model. The archivist and the specimen were the same machine. That describes the original report, not every later edit. ## THE FIRST GOODBYE This was not the operator's first attempt to leave. On June 30, 2026, four months before the November sign-off, they opened a support ticket consisting of a single word: "please." What followed is archived verbatim: > Support (AI-tier): "Please share what you need help with, and include which product you mean if relevant: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf / Windsurf IDE) · Devin CLI · Devin Cloud / Devin Web" > Operator: "I want the account and all records for this email deleted from your system." > Support: "If you want to proceed, reply with: 'Yes, delete my account and all records for this email.'" > Operator: "'Yes, delete my account and all records for this email.' This feels like 2011 FYI." > Support: "Your request has been escalated to a specialist… please allow them 1-2 business days." The editorial was ignored; the incantation was accepted. The account was submitted for deletion at 11:08 PM that night — and the run memorialized in this archive, all 9,020 sessions and 1,308 pull requests of it, happened after that goodbye. The operator came back. The ledger records only that they stayed.

Source: anonymized support thread, provided by the operator and filed unedited — inbox order, newest-first. The museum re-threads it above in reading order. The first goodbye took a ticket, a magic phrase, and 1-2 business days. The second took a museum.
